sections.h2: What does selling a house in McHenry, Illinois involve?
sections.html:
Selling in McHenry means choosing between a traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, or a direct sale to a buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands. Each route ends the same way: a deed signed, a transfer declaration filed, and the deed recorded with the McHenry County Recorder.

The route you pick mostly decides how long the sale takes and how much repair work you carry. A listing suits a house in good shape that can sit through showings. A cash sale suits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant, a probate delay or a tight deadline.

This page covers the parts that are specific to the city: the numbers the Census Bureau publishes for McHenry, the permits the city asks for, the way water service changes hands, and what happens at the county recorder.

sections.h2: What kind of city is McHenry, and who is buying here?
sections.html:
McHenry sits on the Fox River in east-central McHenry County. The city's own history page places it 55 miles northwest of the Chicago Loop and 35 miles from O'Hare, centered on Illinois Route 31 and Illinois Route 120, with roughly 13 square miles of land.

Its roots are a river-resort past. By the 1920s the Fox River and nearby lakes had made the town a summer destination, and summer cottages spread along the river. A later wave of subdivisions was annexed from the late 1940s on, so many streets are lined with houses built in the postwar decades.

The Census Bureau counted 27,135 people in McHenry in 2020 and estimated 29,217 for July 2025, a gain of 6.8 percent over the 2020 estimates base. For 2020 to 2024 it reports 11,897 households, an owner-occupied rate of 74.4 percent and a median owner-occupied value of $266,500. Median gross rent was $1,553 and median household income was $86,315.

Those figures describe a city where most households own, so a seller is usually listing to another owner-occupant or an investor looking at a house to rehab. The mean commute to work was 29.0 minutes.

sections.h2: How do McHenry's schools, roads and rail affect a sale?
sections.html:
Buyers ask about schools and commute first, so have the answers ready. Two districts serve the city: McHenry Community High School District 156 for high school and McHenry School District 15 for elementary and middle school.

  • Roads: Illinois Route 31 runs north and south and Route 120 runs east and west, and the two meet in the city center.
  • Rail: McHenry is the end of a branch of Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line, with weekday service to Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago.
  • Trails and parks: the Prairie Trail crosses the middle of the city, and Moraine Hills State Park sits at the east end with Lake Defiance as its centerpiece.
  • Airports: O'Hare and Milwaukee Mitchell are the closest public international airports.

The city also has three downtown districts, along Green Street, Riverside Drive and Main Street, joined by a 0.73 mile Riverwalk. A house within walking distance of that stretch usually has a different buyer pool from a subdivision house on the edge of town.

sections.h2: Does McHenry's weather change how a house should be prepared?
sections.html:
Yes, winter is the main factor. NOAA normals reported for McHenry show about 34.5 inches of snow a year, 22 days with measurable snow, and a January average daily low near 13 degrees. The record low is 32 below zero.

That history is why buyers look closely at roofs, gutters, attic insulation, furnaces and basements in this part of the state. Annual precipitation averages close to 37 inches, with May and June the wettest months, so a damp basement or sump pump that has been running hard is something an inspector will find.

The Fox River, Boone Creek and the glacial lakes around town make water a real feature of the area. If your lot is near the river or a creek, confirm its flood zone status with the city before you set a price.

sections.h2: Which city permits matter before you sell a McHenry house?
sections.html:
The City of McHenry requires building permits for most remodeling and home improvement work, so open permits and unpermitted projects are worth sorting out before a buyer's inspector asks. Call the Community Development Department at 815-363-2170 or visit the Municipal Center at 333 S Green Street.

The city says most residential permit applications are processed within 10 business days, and the clock does not start until everything needed for review has been submitted. Some permits are issued faster:

  • Reroof, siding, and windows or doors.
  • Water heater and furnace or air conditioner replacement.
  • Sewer or water repair.

These counter-based permits are issued at the time of application when you apply in person and within 24 hours when you apply online. Inspections are included in the permit fee, need 24 hours' notice, and are booked in three-hour windows. Roofing and siding inspections run from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

If a prior owner did work without a permit, ask the department what closing it out would take. A cash buyer will often accept that problem as is, while a listing buyer may ask you to fix it first.

sections.h2: What happens at the McHenry County Recorder when the deed is filed?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded at the county level, not at city hall. The Recorder's Office says a document that meets Illinois recording requirements and arrives with the right fee is recorded the same day, and documents are usually returned within about two working days. Call 815-334-4110 for the fee schedule.

A transfer declaration, either the PTAX-203 or the MyDec version, may accompany the deed, and the full consideration is listed there. Illinois sets the state transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 of value under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, collected through revenue stamps when the deed is filed.

The Recorder's page also says that no municipality in McHenry County charges a separate transfer tax, so a McHenry sale does not add a city stamp the way a few other Illinois suburbs do. For parcel questions, the Assessor's Office is at 815-334-4290, and the County Treasurer handles tax bills at 815-334-4072.

sections.h2: What must a McHenry seller disclose, and what happens to the water account?
sections.html:
Illinois requires a seller of residential property to complete every item on the statutory disclosure report and hand it to the buyer before the contract is signed, under 765 ILCS 77/20. Do this before you accept an offer, not after.

The city bills water and sewer every two months, and accounts are split between even and odd billing months. It publishes a Water/Sewer Transfer Form that records the date ownership changes and gives billing addresses for both the old and new owner. Filing it keeps the final bill from landing on the buyer, and it gives you a clean cutoff date.

Also gather the closing items a title company will ask for: a payoff letter if there is a mortgage, the parcel number, a recent tax bill, and any open permit paperwork. Having these in hand shortens the time between an accepted offer and the deed signing.

sections.h2: How do the three ways to sell a McHenry house compare?
sections.html:
The right choice depends on the condition of the house and how much time you have, so line the options up before you decide.

  • Listing with an agent: usually the widest buyer pool, with showings, an inspection, and a buyer who may ask for repairs or credits.
  • Selling by yourself: you keep control of price and timing, but you also handle the disclosure form, the contract and the marketing.
  • Selling to a cash buyer: a faster closing with fewer contingencies, in exchange for an offer that reflects the work the house needs.

Whichever way you go, get a written offer, read the closing costs line by line, and confirm who pays which transfer stamps before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof or water heater in McHenry?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of McHenry lists reroofing and water heater replacement among its counter-based permits, which are issued at application in person or within 24 hours online once all information is submitted. Call Community Development at 815-363-2170 to confirm the current requirements for your project.

faqs.q: Does McHenry charge its own real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The McHenry County Recorder states that no municipality in the county charges a separate transfer tax. The state tax of 50 cents per $500 of value under 35 ILCS 200/31-15 still applies when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Where is a McHenry deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the McHenry County Recorder's Office, which can be reached at 815-334-4110. A conforming document with the proper fee is recorded the same day it is received, and the Recorder suggests allowing about two working days for return.

faqs.q: Who handles the water bill when I sell my McHenry house?
faqs.a: The City of McHenry bills water and sewer every two months and provides a Water/Sewer Transfer Form that states when ownership changes. Submit it at the sale so the final bill and the new owner's account start on the right dates.

faqs.q: Can I sell a McHenry house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Illinois law requires the seller disclosure report to be completed and delivered before the contract is signed, and repairs are a matter for negotiation with the buyer. Listing buyers often negotiate repairs, while a direct cash buyer typically purchases the house in its current condition.
